title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 3.2 Birth of John the Baptist

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

John the Baptist was born to Zechariah and Elizabeth after an angel spoke in the temple. In this sub-strand you will retell Luke 1:5-13 and 57, then read Luke 1:76-79 to see how John would prepare the way for the Messiah. You will also learn why a righteous life means turning away from sin.

## Strand 3.0: The Life of Jesus Christ
Sub-strand 3.2: Birth of John the Baptist
Suggested lessons: 2

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the Birth of John the Baptist
b) discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah
c) appreciate the need to live a righteous life by turning away from sins

## Key inquiry questions
1. How is John the Baptist a precursor of Jesus Christ?

## Core competencies
• Digital Literacy: the skill of connecting using technology is portrayed as learners watch a video clip on the birth of John the Baptist.

## Values
• Unity: learners work in pairs and groups to perform different tasks.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are reinforced as learners sing and role play.
• English: reading skills are applied as learners read the Holy Bible.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, Sub-strand 3.2 Birth of John the Baptist
• Luke 1:5-13, 57; Luke 1:76-79

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: The promise and the birth

LESSON 1: THE PROMISE AND THE BIRTH
===================================

## What you will learn
• Retell the birth of John the Baptist from Luke 1:5-13 and 57.
• Describe the angel's appearance to Zechariah.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the Birth of John the Baptist

## Introduction
Some families wait many years for a child. Zechariah and Elizabeth had waited. While Zechariah was serving in the temple, an angel told him that their prayer had been heard.

## Notes
Read Luke 1:5-13 and verse 57 in pairs. Retell only those verses.

### Zechariah and Elizabeth
In the time of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah. He belonged to the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was Elizabeth. She also came from the family of Aaron, the priestly family. Both of them were righteous in God's sight. They obeyed the Lord's commands and were blameless. They had no child, because Elizabeth was not able to conceive, and they were both very old.

### The angel in the temple
When Zechariah's division was on duty, he was chosen by lot to go into the temple of the Lord and burn incense. The worshippers were praying outside. An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. Zechariah was startled and gripped with fear.

The angel said, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to call him John."

### The birth
Luke 1:57 says that when it was time for Elizabeth to have her baby, she gave birth to a son. The verses you are reading do not describe the naming ceremony. You already know from verse 13 that the angel said the child was to be called John.

Role-play the temple scene: Zechariah at the altar, the people praying outside, and the angel at the right side of the altar. Keep the fear, the comfort "Do not be afraid," and the promise of a son named John.

## Key words
• priest — a person set apart to serve God in the temple, as Zechariah did
• incense — a spice burned in worship, which Zechariah was chosen to burn
• righteous — living in a way that is right before God

## Activity: Role-play the angel in the temple
You will need: Bible, Space to act
1. In pairs, read Luke 1:5-13 and 57.
2. Role-play the angel's appearance to Zechariah in the temple.
3. Retell the story from the couple's righteousness to the birth of the son.
4. If a video clip on the birth of John the Baptist is available, watch it and check it against the verses.

## Practice
1. Who were John's parents, and why did they have no child?
2. Where did the angel stand, and what did he tell Zechariah?
3. What does Luke 1:57 say happened?

## Summary
• Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous, old, and childless.
• An angel told Zechariah in the temple that they would have a son named John.
• Elizabeth gave birth to a son.

### Answers to practice
1. Zechariah and Elizabeth. They had no child because Elizabeth was not able to conceive, and they were both very old.
2. At the right side of the altar of incense. He said their prayer had been heard, Elizabeth would bear a son, and the son was to be called John.
3. Elizabeth gave birth to a son.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Preparing the way and turning from sin

LESSON 2: PREPARING THE WAY AND TURNING FROM SIN
================================================

## What you will learn
• Explain from Luke 1:76-79 how John prepared the way for the Messiah.
• Appreciate the need to live a righteous life by turning away from sin.

Curriculum outcomes: b) discuss how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah; c) appreciate the need to live a righteous life by turning away from sins

## Introduction
A precursor goes ahead to prepare people for someone greater. Luke 1:76-79 says John would go before the Lord to prepare His way. That Lord is the Messiah, Jesus Christ.

## Notes
After John was born, his father Zechariah spoke about him. Luke 1:76-79 is the part we read. It says:

- The child would be called a prophet of the Most High.
- He would go before the Lord to prepare the way for Him.
- He would give God's people the knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins.
- This would happen because of the tender mercy of God.
- The rising sun would come from heaven to shine on those living in darkness and in the shadow of death.
- He would guide their feet into the path of peace.

### How John prepared the way
He did not come to take the Lord's place. He went before the Lord. He was a prophet who pointed people to salvation and to the forgiveness of sins. He was to lead people out of darkness into the path of peace. In that way he prepared people for the Messiah. The key question asks how John is a precursor of Jesus Christ. A precursor is someone who goes ahead. Verse 76 says John would go on before the Lord to prepare the way for Him.

### A righteous life
Luke 1:6 says Zechariah and Elizabeth were righteous and obeyed God's commands. Verse 77 speaks of forgiveness of sins. A righteous life is not pretending to be perfect. It is turning away from sins and walking in God's commands.

You turn away from sin when you:

- Stop a wrong action, such as lying or stealing.
- Ask God for forgiveness.
- Choose the path of peace instead of quarrels.
- Obey at home and at school.

Appreciate this need. Do not admire sin. Thank God for His tender mercy, and sing a song about John the Baptist, the prophet who prepared the way.

## Key words
• Messiah — the Lord and Saviour whom John prepared people to receive
• precursor — someone who goes ahead to prepare the way
• prophet — a person who speaks God's message, as John was called a prophet of the Most High

## Activity: Read Luke 1:76-79
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Luke 1:76-79 aloud.
2. Tell how John the Baptist prepared the way for the Messiah, using the verses.
3. List sins a learner should turn away from, and the right action that replaces each one.
4. Sing a song about John the Baptist.

## Practice
1. What would John be called, and what would he do before the Lord?
2. Through what would people know salvation, according to Luke 1:77?
3. What does it mean to live a righteous life?

## Summary
• John would go before the Lord as a prophet to prepare His way.
• He would point people to salvation through the forgiveness of sins.
• A righteous life means turning away from sin.

### Answers to practice
1. A prophet of the Most High. He would go before the Lord to prepare the way for Him.
2. Through the forgiveness of their sins.
3. To turn away from sin and obey God's commands.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 3.2 BIRTH OF JOHN THE BAPTIST
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. John's parents were...
   A. Mary and Joseph
   B. Zechariah and Elizabeth
   C. Abram and Sarai
   D. Amnon and Tamar

2. Why were they childless?
   A. They refused to pray
   B. Elizabeth was unable to conceive, and they were very old
   C. They lived outside Israel
   D. The angel forbade children

3. The angel stood...
   A. at the right side of the altar of incense
   B. on a sycamore tree
   C. by the Jordan only
   D. in Pharaoh's palace

4. The child was to be called...
   A. Jesus
   B. John
   C. David
   D. Abraham

5. Luke 1:57 says Elizabeth...

6. John prepared the way for the Messiah by...
   A. taking the Lord's place
   B. going before the Lord and pointing people to forgiveness
   C. cursing the people
   D. hiding in the temple

7. A precursor is someone who...
   A. goes ahead to prepare the way
   B. arrives last
   C. refuses to speak
   D. collects taxes

8. Luke 1:79 says John would guide people's feet into...
   A. the path of war
   B. the path of peace
   C. the vineyards of Timnah
   D. Egypt

9. Zechariah and Elizabeth are called righteous because...
   A. they were young and rich
   B. they obeyed the Lord's commands
   C. they never served in the temple
   D. they asked for a curse

10. Living a righteous life means...
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 3.2 BIRTH OF JOHN THE BAPTIST
========================================

1. B. Zechariah and Elizabeth
   Luke 1:5 names Zechariah the priest and his wife Elizabeth.

2. B. Elizabeth was unable to conceive, and they were very old
   Luke 1:7 gives this reason.

3. A. at the right side of the altar of incense
   Luke 1:11 places the angel at the right side of the altar of incense.

4. B. John
   Luke 1:13 says, "You are to call him John."

5. gave birth to a son.
   That is the birth verse set for this sub-strand.

6. B. going before the Lord and pointing people to forgiveness
   Luke 1:76-77 says he would go before the Lord and give knowledge of salvation through forgiveness of sins.

7. A. goes ahead to prepare the way
   John is a precursor because he went before the Lord.

8. B. the path of peace
   The verse says he would guide their feet into the path of peace.

9. B. they obeyed the Lord's commands
   Luke 1:6 says they observed all the Lord's commands blamelessly.

10. Turning away from sin and obeying God.
   Forgiveness and obedience belong together in this lesson.
